QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.482 on Nov 20, just below the independent, finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.928 measures fit only across scales 8–63. Slopes of 0.462 (8–20) and 0.569 (25–63) suggest one line fits poorly, possibly reflecting crossover. Higher magnitude H=0.774 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability. H rose 0.018/0.027 over 1/5 observations. The prior-30 z-score of +0.165 isn’t a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha=3.378 uses 100 extremes from 1,000 returns, with x_min=0.02046 in absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The idealized independent-return SE=0.338 understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.419/2.985, not a confidence interval. Plateaus are normal when the top 100 stay unchanged.

H/alpha went from 0.520/3.300 (Nov 6) to 0.455/3.380 (Nov 13) to 0.482/3.378 (Nov 20). These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

interpretation.text:

NVDA.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
NVDA’s 252-return DFA H rose from 0.353 (Oct 12) to 0.562 (Nov 20), above the independent finite-variance benchmark of 0.5. R²=0.974 measures fit only at supplied scales. Short/long slopes (0.490/0.677) make one straight-line exponent a poor fit across 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.676 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.038/0.092 over 1/5 observations. It’s 2.82 standard deviations above its prior 30-observation mean. Overlapping windows preclude a significance interpretation.

Hill alpha fell from 2.921 to 2.812 over those dates (1,000 returns, k=99, x_min=0.04449 absolute log-return units). With a suitable model, lower alpha suggests heavier tails; higher suggests thinner. The independent-return SE=0.283 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs yield 3.254/2.824, not confidence bounds. Unchanged extremes can leave alpha flat. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
SPY’s 252-return DFA H was 0.502, near 0.5 for independent, finite-variance returns. R²=0.953 measures fit only on supplied scales. Short/long H (0.472/0.572) indicate a poor single-exponent fit across scales 8–63, possibly crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.717 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.020/0.021 over 1/5 observations. It was 0.43 standard deviations above its prior-30 mean, not a significance test given overlapping windows. H/alpha went from 0.527/3.400 on Nov 6 to 0.502/3.294 on Nov 20.

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years): k=99, x_min=0.01461 in absolute log-return units. Lower alpha suggests heavier tails under a suitable model. Independent-return SE (alpha/√k=0.331) understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs yield 3.223/2.877, not confidence bounds. Alpha can stay flat when new returns miss the top 99. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
